source.author: verg
source.text: At sceleratum exquirere frigus difficile est: piceae tantum taxique nocentes interdum aut hederae pandunt vestigia nigrae.
source.text_original: At sceleratum exquirere frigus / difficile est: piceae tantum taxique nocentes / interdum aut hederae pandunt vestigia nigrae.
source.text_english: But it is difficult to seek out the accursed cold: only the harmful firs and yews, or at times the black ivy, reveal their traces.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: nec hoc miremur in apostolo, si utatur eius linguae consuetudine, in qua natus est et nutritus, cum Uergilius, alter Homerus apud nos, patriae suae sequens consuetudinem sceleratum frigus appellet.
reuse.text_original: nec hoc miremur in apostolo, si utatur eius linguae consuetudine, in qua natus est et nutritus, cum Uergilius, alter Homerus apud nos, patriae suae sequens consuetudinem 'sceleratum' frigus appellet.
reuse.text_english: Let us not be surprised at this in the apostle if he uses the customary usage of the language in which he was born and brought up, when Vergilius, the other Homer among us, following the usage of his native land, calls cold “criminal.”
